solutions.check: bars rebuilt from the blog's numbered answers (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Passing rubbish container, birds on song in gardens

indicators.note: passing over something means leaving it out, so the container word is dropped from the birds

parts.note: an aria is a song in opera

explanation.surface: Someone walking past a dustbin hears birds singing in the gardens.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Passing' looks like walking by, but it means skipping: the bin is dropped from the middle of the birds, and 'on' puts the song after.
explanation.definitionFit: Rosaria is the plural of rosarium, a rose garden, so it stands for gardens planted with roses.

clue.text: Palace leak reported part of the King's speech?

indicators.note: something reported is passed on by word of mouth, so the sound counts here

parts.note: a leak is slang for urination, and a palace one would be royal

explanation.surface: A leaked story from Buckingham Palace concerns what the King said.
explanation.walkthrough: Leak looks like press gossip, but it is slang for a pee.
explanation.definitionFit: The royal we is a monarch's use of 'we' for 'I', so it is literally part of how a king speaks.

clue.text: Organisation foremost in oil prices ever changing

indicators.note: foremost means at the very front, so the first letters of the following words are used

explanation.surface: The body that leads the oil market keeps changing prices.
explanation.definitionFit: OPEC is the Organization of the Petroleum Exporting Countries, the oil producers' cartel.

clue.text: Swift coming from coarse grass with reasonable cover

indicators.note: with a cover means wrapped by it, so the next word goes round the first

parts.note: sane means reasonable, and here it is the cover
alang is a coarse tropical grass

explanation.surface: A quick bird emerges from long rough grass that gives decent shelter.
explanation.walkthrough: Swift is the bird, not an adjective. Alang is a tropical grass found in Chambers.
explanation.definitionFit: The salangane is a cave swiftlet of south-east Asia, whose nests are used for bird's-nest soup.

clue.text: Sugar in spiced brioches Chinese rejected

indicators.note: spicing something up changes it, so these letters are mixed into a new order
rejected means thrown out, so these letters are discarded

parts.note: Ch is the abbreviation for Chinese

explanation.surface: There is sugar in the spiced buns that the Chinese diners sent back.
explanation.walkthrough: Taking CH out of BRIOCHES leaves six letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Ribose is a simple five-carbon sugar, the one found in RNA.

clue.text: Keeper of birds treasuring larks

indicators.note: larks are pranks or capers, so the letters are fooled about with

explanation.surface: A birdkeeper treasures the skylarks in their care.
explanation.walkthrough: Larks look like the birds kept; they are the frolics that shuffle the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: An austringer is a falconer who keeps and trains goshawks and other short-winged hawks.

clue.text: People with degrees retaining university dictionary of Latin

indicators.note: retaining means holding within, so one piece is kept inside the other

parts.note: U is the abbreviation for university

explanation.surface: Graduates keep a Latin dictionary from their university.
explanation.definitionFit: A gradus is a dictionary of Latin prosody, used by students writing Latin verse.

clue.text: Female religious head dumps a bisexual, primarily for another woman

indicators.note: to dump something is to throw it away, so these letters leave the word

parts.note: an abbess heads a community of nuns

indicators.note: primarily means first of all, so only the opening letter of the next word counts

explanation.surface: A mother superior drops a bisexual partner in favour of another woman.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing A and B from the start of ABBESS leaves BESS.
explanation.definitionFit: Bess is a female first name, a pet form of Elizabeth, so it is simply another woman.

clue.text: Romanian coins are in black nickel

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so the first piece goes between the next ones

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils
an are is a metric unit of area, abbreviated A
Ni is the chemical symbol for nickel

explanation.surface: Romanian coins are made of black nickel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Are' is not a verb here but the metric unit of land area.
explanation.definitionFit: Bani is the plural of ban, the Romanian coin worth a hundredth of a leu.

clue.text: Long-distance traveller not a little tired, begins with a joint

indicators.note: not a little of a word means a small part of it, its first letter, is left out

parts.note: a little of the word: its first letter

explanation.surface: A weary long-haul traveller starts out with a bad joint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tired' looks like part of the picture, but only its first letter matters: it is the little taken away from the word for begins.
explanation.definitionFit: A starship is a spacecraft for interstellar travel, about the longest-distance traveller there is.

clue.text: Pulls up for pause probably in music for psalms

definitions.text: pause probably in music for psalms

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means the word reads from the bottom to the top

parts.note: to hale is to drag or pull

explanation.surface: A musician pulls up for a pause in the psalm.
explanation.definitionFit: Selah is a Hebrew word in the Psalms thought to mark a musical pause or rest.

clue.text: Broadcast featuring dancer normally in the background

indicators.note: seed that is broadcast is scattered widely, so the letters are scattered into a new order

explanation.surface: A broadcast show features a dancer who usually stays at the back.
explanation.definitionFit: A figurante is a ballet dancer in the corps who performs as part of a group, not as a soloist.

clue.text: The old record can make you cry

parts.note: ye is an archaic spelling of the

explanation.surface: An old record is so sad that it reduces you to tears.
explanation.definitionFit: A yelp is a sharp cry, as of a dog or a person in sudden pain.

clue.text: Introduction to poet laureate I fancy one with conversational wit

indicators.note: fancy means elaborate or ornamented, so the letters are dressed up in a new order
an introduction is the start, so only the first letter of the next word is used

explanation.surface: A poet laureate admits to fancying someone with a sparkling tongue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I fancy' reads as admiration, but fancy is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Eutrapelia, from Greek, is Aristotle's virtue of ready, pleasant wit in conversation.

clue.text: Seasonal visitor lost in wood

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for lost, as in sports tables

explanation.surface: Father Christmas has got lost in a forest.
explanation.definitionFit: Santal is another name for sandalwood, a fragrant timber.

clue.text: Mahogany cases viewed in one short day across the Channel

indicators.note: something viewed in a place is seen inside it, so these letters sit within the others
short means cut off, so the word loses its final letter

parts.note: ca is a dictionary abbreviation for cases
jour is French for day, France being across the English Channel

explanation.surface: Mahogany boxes spotted on a quick day trip to France.
explanation.walkthrough: JOUR is trimmed to JOU, and the abbreviation for cases goes inside A + JOU: A(CA)JOU.
explanation.definitionFit: Acajou is a name for mahogany, the reddish timber, and also for the cashew tree.

clue.text: Dance on a horse beginning with equestrian whose name I've forgotten

parts.note: a jig is a lively dance
a mare is a female horse

indicators.note: beginning means the first part, so only the opening letter of the next word counts

explanation.surface: A rider dances on a horse, though no one can recall the rider's name.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the whole closing phrase, a description of a thingummy rather than of the rider.
explanation.definitionFit: A jigamaree is a whatsit or thingummy, a word used for something whose proper name escapes you.

clue.text: Group of stars joins in conversation

indicators.note: something said in conversation is heard, not seen, so the sound counts here

explanation.surface: Someone joins a chat, or so it reads.
explanation.definitionFit: Lynx is a faint northern constellation, named after the wild cat.

clue.text: Muslim leader getting about a year set up for South American people

indicators.note: in a down entry, set up means the pieces are raised to read from the bottom

parts.note: an imam leads prayers in a mosque
Y is the abbreviation for year

explanation.surface: A Muslim cleric is appointed for a year to serve a South American community.
explanation.definitionFit: The Yanomami are an indigenous people of the Amazon rainforest in Brazil and Venezuela.

clue.text: No governors initially like entering race that's rather rough

indicators.note: something entering goes into the other word, so it sits inside
no here means without, so the following letter is taken away
initially points to the first letter of the word governors as the one to go

parts.note: dig is slang for like, as in I dig it

explanation.surface: A race run without governors in charge turns rather rough.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Like' is the slang verb, as in 'I dig it'; once it loses its G the remainder enters the word for race.
explanation.definitionFit: Rudish is an old adjective formed from rude, meaning somewhat coarse or rough.

clue.text: End of row Ring seat excites one?

indicators.note: excited things are stirred up, so these letters are agitated into a new order
end of picks out only the last letter of the following word

explanation.surface: A front-row seat at the Ring cycle thrills the opera lover.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the single word 'one', with the question mark: the person excited by a Ring seat. The Ring is Wagner's four-opera cycle.
explanation.definitionFit: A Wagnerist is a devotee of Wagner's music, just the sort of person thrilled by tickets to his operas.

clue.text: Fatty Arbuckle's entry police officer put forward

indicators.note: an entry is the way in, so the opening letter of the word is taken

parts.note: to pose a question is to put it forward

explanation.surface: A police officer advances a case involving Fatty Arbuckle, the silent-film comedian.
explanation.walkthrough: Fatty Arbuckle was a silent-film star tried for manslaughter; here 'Fatty' is split off as the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Adipose means consisting of or relating to fat, as in adipose tissue.

clue.text: Forced to go to sea, Asian people getting Government help around end of month

indicators.note: around means encircling, so the earlier pieces wrap round the following letter

parts.note: the Shan are a people of Myanmar
G is the abbreviation for government

indicators.note: end of picks out only the last letter of the following word

explanation.surface: Asians compelled to work at sea receive government help at the month's end.
explanation.walkthrough: The Shan are a people of Myanmar; the month's last letter is wrapped by the help that follows.
explanation.definitionFit: To shanghai someone was to drug or trick them into serving as a sailor, so shanghaied men were forced to sea.

clue.text: Philosopher's follower hard on old Manc uni

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils
UMIST was the University of Manchester Institute of Science and Technology, merged in 2004

explanation.surface: A philosophy disciple was tough on a former Manchester university.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry 'on' places the first piece above the second. Manc is slang for Mancunian, from Manchester.
explanation.definitionFit: A Humist is a follower of David Hume, the Scottish philosopher.

clue.text: Hideous deep wound left, ending with surgery

parts.note: a gash is a deep cut
L is the abbreviation for left

indicators.note: ending with points to the final letter of the following word

explanation.surface: An ugly deep cut was left, ending in an operation.
explanation.definitionFit: Gashly is an old variant of ghastly, meaning frightful or hideous.

clue.text: Make stronger sheep fencing unit

indicators.note: fencing encloses a field, so one word is placed inside the other

explanation.surface: A farmer strengthens a sheep pen around a single animal.
explanation.walkthrough: Tup is the northern English word for a ram.
explanation.definitionFit: To tone up muscles or a body is to make them firmer and stronger through exercise.

clue.text: China supporting case of Turkey representative

indicators.note: the case of a word is its outside, so only its first and last letters are kept

parts.note: china is rhyming slang for mate (china plate), so a pal

explanation.surface: Chinaware sits on a crate from Turkey, the typical sample.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry 'supporting' puts China below the case of Turkey. China plate is Cockney rhyming slang for mate.
explanation.definitionFit: Typal means typical or representative of a type.

clue.text: Warriors clear, marches are banned

indicators.note: marches are borders, and banning them strips off the word's outer letters

parts.note: limpid means clear, as of water

explanation.surface: Soldiers make it plain that protest marches are prohibited.
explanation.walkthrough: Marches are border lands, so 'marches are banned' strips the outer L and D from LIMPID.
explanation.definitionFit: An impi is a body of Zulu warriors, a regiment in the Zulu army.

clue.text: Index estimated by head of finance tipped

indicators.note: tipped means tilted right over, so the letters are upended and read from the bottom

parts.note: est. is the abbreviation for estimated

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A stock index estimated by the finance chief is tipped to rise.
explanation.definitionFit: The FTSE 100 is the London stock market's main share index.

clue.text: Terms on Clyde preposterous, fish in sharp decline

indicators.note: a term is an end point, so the last letters of the next two words are taken

parts.note: a carp is a freshwater fish

explanation.surface: Absurd conditions on the River Clyde have caused fish stocks to plummet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On' puts the two end letters before the fish.
explanation.definitionFit: An escarp is a steep slope or escarpment, the sharp fall of ground below a ridge.

clue.text: Strip of material in stretched corset without lines

indicators.note: without means lacking, so the named letters are taken out

parts.note: a roll-on is an elasticated corset or girdle
L is the abbreviation for line, so two of them stand for lines

explanation.surface: A strip of fabric sits in a stretchy corset with no seams.
explanation.definitionFit: Roon is a Scots word for a strip or selvage of cloth.

clue.text: After indisposition one's sucked?

parts.note: past means after, as in half past

indicators.note: sucked means drawn out, so the letter for one is pulled away

parts.note: an ail is an ailment or indisposition

explanation.surface: Once you have been ill, a lozenge is what you suck.
explanation.walkthrough: Chambers gives indisposition as a sense of the noun ail. Read whole, the clue describes a lozenge sucked after a bout of illness.
explanation.definitionFit: A pastil, or pastille, is a medicated sweet or lozenge, sucked to soothe a sore throat.

clue.text: Stop in Aberdeen and Leith announced

indicators.note: something announced is spoken aloud, so the sound of the name counts here

parts.note: Prue Leith is a cookery writer and Bake Off judge, so Leith stands for her first name

explanation.surface: A train stops at Aberdeen and Leith, as the station announcer says.
explanation.walkthrough: Aberdeen and Leith are both Scottish places, but Leith here is Prue Leith, judge on The Great British Bake Off.
explanation.definitionFit: Proo is a Scots call to a horse to halt, so it is a word for stop in Scotland.

clue.text: A bass seen in Dart likely to be lost!

indicators.note: something seen in another thing is inside it, so these letters go within

parts.note: a dart is a small thrown missile
B is the abbreviation for bass in music

explanation.surface: A sea bass spotted in the River Dart is in danger of disappearing.
explanation.walkthrough: The Dart is a Devon river, but here it is a thrown missile; B goes inside: A + MISS(B)ILE.
explanation.definitionFit: Amissible is a rare adjective meaning liable to be lost, from Latin amittere, to lose.

clue.text: March with smooth easy movement, wanting Grenadier's lead

indicators.note: wanting means lacking, so the word goes without the named letter

parts.note: a glide is a smooth, effortless movement
the leading letter of the word Grenadier

explanation.surface: Soldiers march gracefully, minus the Grenadier who should head them.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is March the month, not the soldiers' step.
explanation.definitionFit: Lide is an old dialect name for the month of March.

clue.text: Oil refinery feedstock, namely for cracking and ending in gasoline?

definitions.text: Oil refinery feedstock, namely for cracking and ending in gasoline?

indicators.note: a word put up for cracking is broken apart, so its letters are rearranged
ending in picks out only the last letter of the following word

explanation.surface: Refinery feedstock oil is cracked and ends up as petrol.
explanation.walkthrough: Cracking is the refinery process that breaks heavy oils into lighter ones such as gasoline, so the whole clue also describes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Amylene is pentene, a hydrocarbon made in and fed through refinery cracking units on the way to petrol blends.
